description: Found reviewing defk-upc + defk-n4r.10 together. With out = alloc(u8, 2 * len(a)) and for i <- 0..(len(a) - 1)//1 do out[2 * i] = a[i] end, the write has no bounds check (defk-upc's scaled facts). Written as a reduce accumulator (for ..., reduce: out do o -> o[2 * i] = a[i]; o end) the same write keeps defk_put_u8: reduce_accs/with_acc_facts carry only fin and the constant len_lo into the accumulator, not len_lb (relative/scaled length facts). Defk.Report.print shows 'bounds check kept; nothing proves 2 * i < len(o)'. Matters for the table-building loops (1BRC defk-n4r.6, HLL defk-9p6.15, LZ4). Fix: carry len_lb into the accumulator like len_lo, and drop it via with_acc_facts' retry when a new value lacks it (lost_facts?/facts? must learn len_lb, compared soundly: the new value's facts must imply the assumed ones). Done when the reduce form compiles with no bounds check on o[2 * i], a test on the C, a property that a body returning a shorter array (e.g. alloc(u8, len(a))) keeps the check, and agreement passes.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** An array reduce accumulator keeps the relative/scaled length facts (len_lb) of its initial value when every iteration preserves them, so o[2 * i] in the reduce form is check-free like the plain-for form

**Current behavior:**
With `out = alloc(u8, 2 * len(a))`, `for i <- 0..(len(a) - 1)//1 do out[2 * i] = a[i] end` has no bounds check (defk-upc's scaled facts). The same write through a reduce accumulator, `for i <- 0..(len(a) - 1)//1, reduce: out do o -> o[2 * i] = a[i]; o end`, keeps defk_put_u8; the report says "nothing proves 2 * i < len(o)". Accumulator facts carry finiteness and the constant length lower bound (len_lo) but not len_lb.

**Desired behavior:**
- A reduce accumulator starts with its initial value's len_lb facts, as it does for len_lo, and keeps them only if the value each iteration returns provably has them too (the new value's facts imply the assumed ones; otherwise the facts are dropped, by the existing retry for lost facts). Unsound carries are worse than a kept check: when in doubt, drop.
- Applies to accumulators in for-reduce over ranges, including tuple accumulators holding arrays, and nested reduces, as far as the existing len_lo path supports them.

**Key interfaces:**
- The accumulator fact carry and its retry when a body loses facts (compiler); the report's "nothing proves" text stays accurate

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The reduce form above compiles with no bounds check on o[2 * i] (test on the generated C source and the report)
- [ ] Property/test: a body that returns a shorter array (e.g. o2 = alloc(u8, len(a)); o2) keeps the check, and out-of-range writes still raise
- [ ] Agreement (assert_agrees) passes for the new kernels, also under forced yields
- [ ] `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean; note in docs/performance.md if a measured example gains

**Out of scope:**
- New fact kinds (relations between variables: defk-2mz)

title: Array reduce accumulators drop alloc's length facts (len_lb): o[2 * i] keeps its bounds check
